U.S. President Donald Trump said he may travel to Egypt this weekend to finalize a long-awaited Gaza peace deal after President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi publicly invited him to come to Cairo to sign the agreement if negotiations succeed.

President Trump visited Sharm El-Sheikh, Egypt on October 13, 2025, to meet with European and Middle Eastern leaders in what's being billed as an international peace summit, following the start of a US-brokered ceasefire deal to end the war in the Gaza Strip.

More than 20 leaders, including French President Emmanuel Macron and UK Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer, attended the summit in Sharm El-Sheikh.

Leaders or foreign ministers from Germany, France, the UK, Italy, Qatar, the UAE, Jordan, Türkiye, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Indonesia participated in the summit.

The visit appears to have been successful in convening international leaders to discuss the Gaza peace agreement that was brokered by the Trump administration.
